review_scope_note: This is a bounded current-source collision review, not an exhaustive proof of novelty.

sources.title: LEGO-Eval: Towards Fine-Grained Evaluation on Synthesizing 3D Embodied Environments with Tool Augmentation
sources.finding: LEGO-Eval already studies instruction complexity by released constraint count and reports Holistic Success Rate across simple (2-7), moderate (8-12), and complex (>12) groups. It also reports Partial Success Rate by the four constraint types.
sources.implication: A paper whose contribution is merely 'more LEGO constraints cause lower success' is directly collided and must be rejected. Per-type mean difficulty is also not a new contribution.

sources.title: Large Language Models Can Follow Instructions, But Not Many at Once: Phase Transitions in Compositional Constraint Satisfaction
sources.finding: In deterministic-verifier LLM instruction following, compositional degradation is reported to be largely explained by multiplicative accumulation of approximately independent constraint failures, with structural constraints degrading faster than lexical constraints.
sources.implication: The 3D candidate must not assume pairwise interference. Conditional independence / multiplicative accumulation is the strongest conceptual null; a 3D-specific claim survives only if cross-type failure coupling remains after matched load, length, generator, and per-type difficulty controls.

sources.title: GraphDreamer: Compositional 3D Scene Synthesis from Scene Graphs
sources.finding: GraphDreamer explicitly motivates scene graphs as a structured representation for complex multi-object text-to-3D descriptions and relationships.
sources.implication: A generic claim that scene graphs help complex 3D prompts is not a sufficient method contribution. Any later structured intervention must specifically reduce the preregistered coupling residual under same-information controls.

sources.title: InstructScene: Instruction-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis with Semantic Graph Prior
sources.finding: InstructScene already uses a semantic graph prior to improve controllability in instruction-driven indoor scene synthesis.
sources.implication: Semantic-graph conditioning is prior art and can serve only as a mechanism reference/baseline unless a new causal role is isolated.

rejected_theses: constraint count alone is a novel complexity law on LEGO-Bench
different LEGO constraint types have different average difficulty
scene graphs generally help complex 3D generation

surviving_scientific_gap.name: conditional cross-type failure coupling in 3D scene synthesis
surviving_scientific_gap.question: After conditioning on generator identity, instruction length, total constraint count, and flexible additive difficulty for each released constraint type, do per-constraint failures remain dependent across types within the same 3D scene instruction?
surviving_scientific_gap.candidate_signal: positive excess cross-type joint-failure probability or residual dependence, especially for execution-linked type pairs such as Object Selection-Object Placement and Floor Layout-Object Placement
surviving_scientific_gap.entropy_role: constraint-type entropy is a preregistered moderator/stratifier for coupling burden, not the scientific object by itself
surviving_scientific_gap.novelty_caveat: Requires independent formal source review before canonical Generator/ProblemGate admission.
